diazonium-chemistry.q: How is 1,3,5-tribromobenzene made?
diazonium-chemistry.why: The amine directs all three bromines, then H3PO2 deletes it.

diazonium-chemistry.q: What does aniline plus bromine water give?
diazonium-chemistry.why: Strongly activated, so all three positions react without a catalyst.

diazonium-chemistry.q: What intermediate forms when a diazonium salt loses N2?
diazonium-chemistry.why: Badly unstable, which is why it grabs whatever nucleophile is present at once. In warm water that nucleophile is water, and the product is the phenol.

diazonium-chemistry.q: What is the Sandmeyer reaction specifically?
diazonium-chemistry.why: CuCl, CuBr and CuCN are the three standard cases.

diazonium-chemistry.q: Which reaction sequence lets you place a group meta when it would go ortho/para?
diazonium-chemistry.why: Directing effects cannot be argued with, so you change what is doing the directing.

diazonium-chemistry.q: Can an aryl halide be converted to a phenol directly?
diazonium-chemistry.why: An unactivated aryl halide does neither SN1 nor SN2.

diazonium-chemistry.q: Why is diazonium chemistry described as a hub?
options: It is used in every synthesis
diazonium-chemistry.why: A single ring position becomes a socket almost anything can be plugged into.

polymer-basics.q: What is a monomer?
options: The small unit a polymer is built from
The repeating piece inside the chain
polymer-basics.why: The repeating piece inside the chain is the repeat unit, which may differ from the monomer.

polymer-basics.q: What is the degree of polymerization?
polymer-basics.why: For step-growth it is 1/(1-p), where p is the fraction of groups reacted.

polymer-basics.q: How many reactive sites does a chain-forming monomer need?
polymer-basics.why: One stops after a single bond; three or more gives a network.

polymer-basics.q: What does a monomer with three reactive sites give?
polymer-basics.why: Which is what makes a thermoset, and why it cannot be melted.

polymer-basics.q: What does a monomer with one reactive site give?
polymer-basics.why: It makes one bond and is finished.

polymer-basics.q: What is lost in an addition polymerization?
polymer-basics.why: The pi bond simply opens, so the repeat unit matches the monomer.

polymer-basics.q: What is lost in a condensation polymerization?
polymer-basics.why: Which is what the word condensation means.

polymer-basics.q: How do you tell addition from condensation quickly?
polymer-basics.why: A lighter repeat unit means something was expelled; matching formulas mean nothing was, so for an alkene monomer, addition.

polymer-basics.q: Which monomer class gives addition polymers?
polymer-basics.why: The double bond supplies both reactive ends.

polymer-basics.q: Which reaction builds a condensation polymer?
polymer-basics.why: Esterification or amide formation, run repeatedly.

polymer-basics.q: What is a thermoplastic?
polymer-basics.why: Heating lets the chains slide, so it can be melted and remolded.

polymer-basics.q: What is a thermoset?
polymer-basics.why: Heating destroys it rather than softening it, because melting would mean breaking bonds.

polymer-basics.q: Which can be melted and remolded?
polymer-basics.why: A network has nothing to loosen.

polymer-basics.q: What is the repeat unit of polyethylene?
polymer-basics.why: Break the pi bond of ethylene and bracket what is left.

polymer-basics.q: Why does chain length raise melting point?
options: Longer chains have more contact and entangle
polymer-basics.why: More surface in contact means more total intermolecular attraction.

polymer-basics.q: What does branching do to packing?
polymer-basics.why: Which is the whole difference between LDPE and HDPE.

polymer-basics.q: What do cross-links do?
polymer-basics.why: A few make rubber elastic; many make a rigid thermoset.

polymer-basics.q: What does regularity along a chain allow?
polymer-basics.why: Chains that match can lie against each other.

polymer-basics.q: Which grows faster in an addition polymerization?
polymer-basics.why: One active end adds monomer very fast, so long chains exist from the start.

polymer-basics.q: How do chains grow in a step-growth polymerization?
options: Only monomer adds to a chain
polymer-basics.why: Which is why nothing is long until conversion is very high.

polymer-basics.q: What is the degree of polymerization at 99% conversion in a step-growth?
polymer-basics.why: 1/(1-0.99), and 99% sounds finished while giving a marginal material.

polymer-basics.q: What is the degree of polymerization at 90% conversion?
polymer-basics.why: An oil rather than a plastic.

polymer-basics.q: Why does step-growth need exact stoichiometry?
polymer-basics.why: Two like groups cannot react with each other, so growth stops.

polymer-basics.q: Why does a monofunctional impurity matter so much?
polymer-basics.why: A small mole fraction of it wrecks the molecular weight.

polymer-basics.q: Which polymer class is polyethylene?
polymer-basics.why: From an alkene, with nothing lost.

polymer-basics.q: Which polymer class is nylon?
polymer-basics.why: A diacid and a diamine, losing water at each amide.

polymer-basics.q: What is a repeat unit?
polymer-basics.why: It equals the monomer only for addition polymers.

polymer-basics.q: Why is no new reaction needed for this chapter?
polymer-basics.why: Alkene addition and acyl substitution, run on a monomer with two ends.

polymer-basics.q: What does glycerol's three OH groups predict?
polymer-basics.why: Three sites lets each monomer join three others.

polymer-basics.q: Which question predicts the material before any mechanism?
polymer-basics.why: One, two or three or more gives three different outcomes.

addition-polymers.q: What are the three stages of radical polymerization?
addition-polymers.why: The same three as radical halogenation.
It breaks homolytically to give two radicals.

options: The radical adds to the next alkene
addition-polymers.why: Generating a new radical at the end of a longer chain, thousands of times.
Either combining or disproportionating.
So propagation runs a long way before two radicals find each other.

addition-polymers.q: Which end of CH2=CHX does the growing radical attack?
addition-polymers.why: That leaves the radical on the substituted, more stable carbon.
It follows from taking the more stable radical every time.

addition-polymers.q: Which rule does head-to-tail regiochemistry resemble?
addition-polymers.why: Both come from asking which intermediate is more stable.
Foam cups and packaging.

addition-polymers.q: What polymer comes from vinyl chloride?
addition-polymers.why: Pipe, flooring and insulation.
Teflon, and there is no head-to-tail question because both carbons are identical.

addition-polymers.q: What polymer comes from methyl methacrylate?
addition-polymers.why: Plexiglas, and it is transparent because it is amorphous.

options: How substituents are arranged along the chain
addition-polymers.why: Each substituted backbone carbon has a fixed orientation, and tacticity names the pattern they make.
Packs well, so the material is crystalline and strong.
Regular, so it packs well too.
Cannot pack, so the material is amorphous and soft.

addition-polymers.q: What tacticity does radical polymerization give?
options: It alternates strictly along the chain
addition-polymers.why: A planar radical has no strong preference about which face the next monomer arrives on.
It holds the chain on a metal center so every addition happens the same way.
Nothing packs, so there is no strength.

addition-polymers.q: How does branching happen in radical polymerization?
addition-polymers.why: The chain then continues from that point, leaving a branch.
High-pressure radical polymerization does this constantly.
A Ziegler-Natta catalyst suppresses the backbiting that makes branches.
Branched, badly packed and flexible.
Linear, well packed and rigid.

addition-polymers.q: Do LDPE and HDPE have the same formula?
addition-polymers.why: Same monomer, same repeat unit, different architecture.

addition-polymers.q: How do you draw an addition polymer from its monomer?
addition-polymers.why: Then write a bond leaving each side of the bracket.

options: Radical polymerization places the phenyls at random
Phenyl groups are too bulky to pack
Its chains are too short to form crystals
addition-polymers.why: Syndiotactic polystyrene has the same phenyl group and is crystalline, melting near 270 C, so bulk is not the cause. Atacticity is.

addition-polymers.q: What kind of polymerization suits an alkene with donating groups?
addition-polymers.why: The growing cation has to be stabilized.

addition-polymers.q: What kind of polymerization suits an alkene with withdrawing groups?
addition-polymers.why: The mirror image of the cationic case.

addition-polymers.q: What does a Ziegler-Natta catalyst control?
addition-polymers.why: Holding the chain at a defined metal site does both at once.

condensation-polymers.q: What does a diacid plus a diol give?
condensation-polymers.why: Losing water at each ester bond.

condensation-polymers.q: What does a diacid plus a diamine give?
condensation-polymers.why: Losing water at each amide bond.

condensation-polymers.q: What is PET made from?
condensation-polymers.why: The drinks bottle and the polyester shirt.

condensation-polymers.q: What is nylon 6,6 made from?
condensation-polymers.why: First number the diamine's carbons, second the diacid's: hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid.

condensation-polymers.q: What do the numbers in nylon 6,6 count?
condensation-polymers.why: Six in the diacid and six in the diamine, readable straight from the name.

condensation-polymers.q: What is Kevlar made from?
condensation-polymers.why: Both aromatic and both para-substituted, which is what makes the chains straight.

condensation-polymers.q: Why is Kevlar so strong?
condensation-polymers.why: Three factors compounding, none of them exotic.

condensation-polymers.q: Which resists hydrolysis better?
options: It depends on the chain length
condensation-polymers.why: Amides are the least reactive acyl derivative, which carries over to the material.

condensation-polymers.q: Why is PET chemically recyclable?
options: Its ester bonds can be hydrolyzed back to monomers
condensation-polymers.why: The property that makes it less durable is what makes it recoverable.

condensation-polymers.q: What comparison does a polyamide invite?
condensation-polymers.why: Same amide, same planarity, same interchain hydrogen bonding.

condensation-polymers.q: Nylon is strong for the same reason as which biological structure?
condensation-polymers.why: Backbone hydrogen bonds between neighboring chains.

condensation-polymers.q: What is a polyurethane made from?
condensation-polymers.why: The alcohol adds across the N=C=O group.

condensation-polymers.q: What is unusual about polyurethane formation?
condensation-polymers.why: Which is why the class is properly called step-growth rather than condensation.

condensation-polymers.q: Why is the class called step-growth rather than condensation?
options: It grows in steps of ten
It is a newer name only
condensation-polymers.why: Polyurethane is the exception that forces the broader name.

condensation-polymers.q: What linkage does a polycarbonate have?
condensation-polymers.why: Two oxygens on one carbonyl.

condensation-polymers.q: What is polycarbonate used for?
condensation-polymers.why: Transparent and extremely impact-resistant.

condensation-polymers.q: What is the formula for degree of polymerization in step-growth?
condensation-polymers.why: Which is why the last tenth of a percent is where the material appears.

condensation-polymers.q: At 99.9% conversion, what is the degree of polymerization?
condensation-polymers.why: And 99% gives only 100, which is barely a plastic.

condensation-polymers.q: Why must the water be removed continuously?
options: To drive the equilibrium to completion
To prevent hydrolysis of the monomer
condensation-polymers.why: Every step is an equilibrium, and the reaction has to be driven the whole way.

condensation-polymers.q: What happens with a 2% excess of one monomer?
condensation-polymers.why: Two like groups cannot react with each other, so growth halts.

condensation-polymers.q: Which polymer is made from lactic acid?
condensation-polymers.why: One monomer carrying both an OH and a COOH.

condensation-polymers.q: Why can lactic acid polymerize with itself?
options: It has both an OH and a COOH
condensation-polymers.why: Two reactive sites is the only requirement, and they need not be the same kind.

condensation-polymers.q: What bond does PET's backbone contain?
condensation-polymers.why: Which is the handle that hydrolysis can select.

condensation-polymers.q: Why does para substitution matter in Kevlar?
options: It makes the ring more reactive
condensation-polymers.why: A straight chain lets neighbors touch along their whole length.

condensation-polymers.q: How many reactive groups does each condensation monomer need?
condensation-polymers.why: The same rule as every chain polymer.

condensation-polymers.q: What kind of reaction forms each join?
condensation-polymers.why: Esterification or amide formation, and nothing else.

condensation-polymers.q: Why does polyester fabric lose strength in hot alkali faster than nylon?
options: Esters hydrolyze more readily than amides
condensation-polymers.why: The acyl reactivity ladder applied to a material. It is not a blanket ranking: nylon is the one attacked by acid, chlorine and sunlight.

condensation-polymers.q: What does 90% conversion give in a step-growth?
condensation-polymers.why: Which is why these reactions are run to a completeness that looks excessive.

condensation-polymers.q: Is Kevlar a thermoset?
condensation-polymers.why: No cross-links, so not a network. It has no melt either, decomposing near 500 C and spun from solution.

condensation-polymers.q: What are the two monomers of a polyester, read backwards?
condensation-polymers.why: Cut the acyl C-O bond, leaving the oxygen on the alcohol side, and check each fragment has two reactive sites.

polymer-properties.q: What are crystalline regions in a polymer?
polymer-properties.why: Almost every real polymer has both crystalline and amorphous regions.

polymer-properties.q: What does higher crystallinity do to density?
polymer-properties.why: Packed chains occupy less space.

polymer-properties.q: Why is a highly crystalline polymer opaque?
options: Crystalline and amorphous regions scatter light
polymer-properties.why: Their refractive indices differ, so light scatters at every boundary.

polymer-properties.q: Which polymers are used for windows?
polymer-properties.why: No crystalline regions means nothing to scatter light.

polymer-properties.q: What is Tg?
polymer-properties.why: Essentially every polymer has one; only semicrystalline ones also have a Tm.

polymer-properties.q: What is Tm?
polymer-properties.why: A fully amorphous polymer has no Tm at all.

polymer-properties.q: Which transition does every polymer have?
polymer-properties.why: Because every polymer has amorphous regions.

polymer-properties.q: Why does rubber shatter in liquid nitrogen?
polymer-properties.why: Below Tg the chains are frozen and cannot deform.

polymer-properties.q: Why is rubber elastic at room temperature?
polymer-properties.why: Its amorphous chains are mobile, and the cross-links pull them back.

polymer-properties.q: What is vulcanization?
polymer-properties.why: Short S-S bridges form between the chains.

polymer-properties.q: What does a few percent of cross-links give?
polymer-properties.why: Chains can stretch apart and are pulled back, which is a tire.

polymer-properties.q: What does heavy cross-linking give?
polymer-properties.why: Nothing can move at all.

polymer-properties.q: What is rubber with no cross-links like?
polymer-properties.why: Chains slide past each other permanently.

polymer-properties.q: Why is rubber elasticity an entropy effect?
polymer-properties.why: Releasing it lets entropy pull the chains back into a coil.

polymer-properties.q: What happens to a stretched rubber band when heated?
polymer-properties.why: The entropic restoring force scales with temperature, unlike almost every other material.

polymer-properties.q: Why does a rubber band warm when stretched?
polymer-properties.why: The standard demonstration that the elasticity is entropic.

polymer-properties.q: What holds a thermoplastic together?
polymer-properties.why: Which heat can overcome, so the chains slide and it can be remolded.

polymer-properties.q: What holds a thermoset together?
polymer-properties.why: One network, so melting would mean breaking bonds.

polymer-properties.q: Which is recyclable by melting?
polymer-properties.why: A network has nothing to loosen.

polymer-properties.q: Give an example of a thermoset.
polymer-properties.why: Bakelite and vulcanized rubber are others.

polymer-properties.q: What do bulky side groups do?
polymer-properties.why: They raise Tg and slow crystallization. In polystyrene the random placement is what actually prevents packing.

polymer-properties.q: What do interchain hydrogen bonds do?
polymer-properties.why: Nylon and Kevlar both depend on them.

polymer-properties.q: Which argument from the biomolecules chapter does packing repeat?
polymer-properties.why: Straight chains stack and melt high; kinked or branched ones do not.

polymer-properties.q: What does more crystallinity do to transparency?
polymer-properties.why: Scattering at the boundaries between regions is what causes the cloudiness.

polymer-properties.q: Which has a sharp melting point?
polymer-properties.why: Amorphous material softens over a range instead.

polymer-properties.q: What does a long flexible spacer do to Tg?
polymer-properties.why: More mobility in the chain means less energy needed to unfreeze it.

polymer-properties.q: Why is HDPE rigid?
options: It has a higher formula weight
polymer-properties.why: The same repeat unit as LDPE, arranged differently.

polymer-properties.q: What does stretching do to a polymer's chains?
polymer-properties.why: Which is also how fibers are drawn to increase strength.

polymer-properties.q: Which property does crystallinity NOT increase?
polymer-properties.why: It reduces transparency, because ordered regions scatter light.

polymer-properties.q: How many transition temperatures can a polymer have?
polymer-properties.why: Tg for the amorphous regions and Tm for the crystalline ones.

polymer-design.q: A polymer backbone contains only carbons. What was the monomer?
polymer-design.why: Put the double bond back into the repeat unit.

polymer-design.q: A polymer backbone contains esters. What were the monomers?
polymer-design.why: Cut the acyl C-O bond of each ester: OH to the acid side, H to the alcohol side.

polymer-design.q: A polymer backbone contains amides. What were the monomers?
polymer-design.why: Cut every amide C-N bond.

polymer-design.q: A disconnection gives a fragment with one reactive group. What does that mean?
options: You cut in the wrong place
polymer-design.why: Every chain-forming monomer must have two, which is what let it join on both sides.

polymer-design.q: How do you check a polyester disconnection by atom count?
options: Monomers minus repeat unit should be two waters
polymer-design.why: One water per ester bond, and a diacid-plus-diol repeat unit has two. PET: 166 + 62 - 192 = 36.

polymer-design.q: Which feature gives high strength?
polymer-design.why: Rigid, straight chains that align along their whole length.

polymer-design.q: Which feature gives hydrolytic resistance?
polymer-design.why: Amides are the least reactive acyl derivative.

polymer-design.q: Which feature gives flexibility?
polymer-design.why: Both lower Tg and prevent packing.

polymer-design.q: Which feature gives transparency?
polymer-design.why: Crystalline regions scatter light at every boundary.

polymer-design.q: Which feature gives a shape that cannot be melted?
polymer-design.why: Three reactive sites gives a network.

polymer-design.q: Which feature gives degradability?
polymer-design.why: They hydrolyze, and enzymes can reach them.

polymer-design.q: Why do durability and persistence go together?
options: Both come from an unreactive backbone
polymer-design.why: The honest version of the plastics problem rather than a failure of chemistry.

polymer-design.q: What is mechanical recycling?
polymer-design.why: Thermoplastics only, and each cycle shortens the chains a little.

polymer-design.q: What is chemical recycling?
polymer-design.why: It needs a backbone bond that can be cleaved selectively.

polymer-design.q: Which plastic is most chemically recyclable?
polymer-design.why: Its ester bonds are a handle hydrolysis can select.

polymer-design.q: Why is polyethylene not chemically recyclable?
polymer-design.why: No bond hydrolysis can pick out from any other. Cracking it back to feedstock works, but that is pyrolysis, not selective cleavage.

polymer-design.q: Why can a thermoset not be recycled either way?
polymer-design.why: The hardest case at end of life.

polymer-design.q: What does PLA hydrolyze back to?
polymer-design.why: An ordinary metabolite, which is what makes it compostable.

polymer-design.q: What is the qualifier on PLA's biodegradability?
polymer-design.why: Biodegradable is a claim about conditions as much as about structure.

polymer-design.q: What decides whether a polymer can be chemically recycled?
polymer-design.why: One functional group is the whole difference.

polymer-design.q: What does each mechanical recycling cycle do?
polymer-design.why: Which is why mechanically recycled material degrades with reuse.

polymer-design.q: Which backbone is a handle for hydrolysis?
polymer-design.why: An amide is one too, though a more resistant one.

polymer-design.q: When was a polymer's end of life decided?
polymer-design.why: The backbone functional group is fixed by the monomer.

polymer-design.q: Which polymer can be both recycled and composted?
polymer-design.why: A polyester that hydrolyzes to a metabolite.

polymer-design.q: Why is a polyolefin so persistent?
polymer-design.why: The properties that make it cheap and inert make it permanent.

polymer-design.q: What must every fragment of a correct disconnection have?
polymer-design.why: That is the self-check that catches an error without knowing the compound.

polymer-design.q: Which property argues against crystallinity?
polymer-design.why: The other three all improve with crystallinity.

polymer-design.q: What does an amorphous rigid polymer get its rigidity from?
polymer-design.why: PMMA through bulky side groups; polycarbonate through rigid bisphenol A units in the backbone.

polymer-design.q: Which monomer would you add to make a thermoset?
polymer-design.why: A third reactive site lets chains tie to each other.

polymer-design.q: What is the honest summary of the plastics problem?
polymer-design.why: You cannot have an inert, durable material that also disappears.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Adding water across a C=O gives what kind of product?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Two OH groups end up on the one former carbonyl carbon.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: A gem-diol is more commonly called a:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: The common name records where it came from, not its structure.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Which carbonyl is the least hydrated at equilibrium?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Only about 0.1%, since two methyls both crowd and feed the carbon.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Acetaldehyde's percent hydrate is closest to:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: One methyl instead of two puts it halfway between formaldehyde and acetone.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Which hydrate is stable enough to isolate?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Its equilibrium sits essentially all the way over.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Why is chloral almost completely hydrated?
options: The chlorines donate electron density to carbon
The chlorines strengthen the C=O bond
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Three of them pulling makes the carbonyl carbon badly electron poor.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: What happens to the carbonyl carbon during hydration?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: A flat carbon turns pyramidal, which is why crowding matters.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Hydration squeezes the substituent angles from about 120 degrees to:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Tetrahedral geometry, and groups that were comfortable at 120 no longer are.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Why do two methyls disfavor the hydrate more than two hydrogens?
options: They block the oxygen lone pairs
They crowd the new sp3 carbon
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Hydrogens have almost nothing to give up when the angle closes.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Alkyl groups affect a carbonyl by:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: That donation stabilizes the starting material, so it has less reason to react.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Toward nucleophiles, the reactivity order is:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Sterics and electronics point the same way, and the hydration table measures it.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Which two factors set the hydration equilibrium?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: The same pair sets every carbonyl reactivity order in the chapter.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Why does aqueous Cr(VI) carry a primary alcohol past the aldehyde?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: The gem-diol is an alcohol again, so the oxidant attacks a second time.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Why does PCC stop at the aldehyde?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: No water means no hydrate, and nothing left with an O-H to attack.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Cyanide adds to a carbonyl to give:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Attack at carbon, then protonation of the alkoxide.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: A cyanohydrin carbon carries which two groups?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: One came from the old carbonyl oxygen, the other from cyanide.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: What makes cyanohydrin formation worth doing synthetically?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Hydration and bisulfite addition build no new carbon skeleton.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Cyanohydrin formation is run near what pH?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Both forms of the reagent have to be present at once.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Why is that pH range chosen?
options: Both CN- and HCN are present
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: CN- does the attacking and HCN protonates the alkoxide.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Hydrolyzing a cyanohydrin's nitrile gives:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: The nitrile becomes the acid and the OH is already in place.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Reducing a cyanohydrin with LiAlH4 gives:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: The nitrile carbon becomes CH2NH2, one carbon away from the OH.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Which step turns a cyanohydrin into an unsaturated nitrile?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Losing the OH and an adjacent hydrogen conjugates the nitrile.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: A cyanohydrin extends the carbon chain by how many carbons?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: And that one carbon arrives with a functional group already on it.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Carbon dioxide plus a Grignard reagent gives:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Another one-carbon extension, chosen for what it leaves behind.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: A nitrile plus a Grignard reagent gives:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Same one-carbon logic, different functional group at the end.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Sodium bisulfite adds to a carbonyl to give:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Solid and water soluble, which is exactly what makes it handy.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Why is the bisulfite adduct useful?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Filter off the solid, then regenerate the carbonyl.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: Which of these will not form a bisulfite adduct?
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: The same crowding that keeps hindered ketones from hydrating.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: The bisulfite adduct is reversed by:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Reversibility is the point, since you want the carbonyl back.

hydrates-cyanohydrins.q: A ketone bearing three fluorines on the next carbon would hydrate:
hydrates-cyanohydrins.why: Fluorine pulls like chlorine does in chloral.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: An aldehyde is readily oxidized to:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: It is the one carbonyl in the chapter still able to climb a rung.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Why do ordinary oxidants leave ketones untouched?
options: The C=O bond is too weak
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Two carbons sit there instead, and a C-C bond would have to break.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Oxidation at a carbon means:
options: Trading a C-H for a C-O
Trading a C-O for a C-H
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The same hydrogen bookkeeping that ranked the alcohols.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Which species is actually oxidized when an aldehyde becomes an acid?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: A bare carbonyl carbon has no hydroxyl for an oxidant to grip.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: The gem-diol can be oxidized because it is:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: It has an OH and an H on the same carbon, like a primary alcohol.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Why does PCC stop at the aldehyde?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Anhydrous dichloromethane keeps the second oxidation from ever starting.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Jones reagent takes a primary alcohol to:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Water in the flask keeps regenerating the hydrate.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Tollens' reagent contains which metal ion?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Held in solution by ammonia under basic conditions.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: The active species in Tollens' reagent is:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The diammine complex keeps silver soluble in base.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Under Tollens' conditions the aldehyde ends up as:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The solution is basic, so the acid is deprotonated as it forms.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: A positive Tollens' test looks like:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Metallic silver plating out on clean glass.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: In a Tollens' test the silver(I) is:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The aldehyde is what gets oxidized, so silver has to go the other way.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: What makes Tollens' useful as a test?
options: It oxidizes alcohols and alkenes too
aldehyde-oxidation.why: A reagent that picks out one group and skips its neighbors.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Why is Tollens' not used to prepare carboxylic acids?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Cost, not chemistry, is what keeps it a test.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Fehling's solution holds Cu(II) with which ligand?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Benedict's is the one built on citrate.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Why does fructose give a positive Benedict's test?
options: Base isomerizes it to an aldose
Its ring cannot open at all
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Through an enediol, which is why a free anomeric carbon rather than an aldehyde is the real test.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: A positive Fehling's or Benedict's test shows:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The red solid drops out of the blue solution that was there before.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Before reaction, a Benedict's solution is what color?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Cu(II) in solution, which is why the red precipitate is easy to see.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Which reagent pair is more robust and used clinically?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Citrate holds the copper better than tartrate does.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Fehling's solution is unreliable with:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Aliphatic aldehydes are the case it handles well.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Why does glucose test positive although it is drawn as a ring?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Opening exposes the aldehyde the ring drawing hides.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: How much open-chain aldehyde does glucose hold at equilibrium?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: Delivered continuously, and consumed as fast as it appears.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: A sugar is called reducing because of:
options: What it does to the metal
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The sugar is in fact the thing being oxidized.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Why is sucrose not a reducing sugar?
aldehyde-oxidation.why: The glycosidic bond ties up both anomeric carbons, and a free one is what a positive test needs.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Lactose and maltose test positive because each:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: One ring can still open and deliver an aldehyde.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Aldehydes oxidize in air by:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: No added reagent is needed at all.

aldehyde-oxidation.q: An old bottle of benzaldehyde grows crystals of:

aldehyde-oxidation.q: How should aldehydes be stored?

aldehyde-oxidation.q: Oxidizing a ketone requires:

aldehyde-oxidation.q: The Baeyer-Villiger converts a ketone to:
aldehyde-oxidation.why: An oxygen is inserted into one of the C-C bonds.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: By-products of the SOCl2 route to an acid chloride?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Oxalyl chloride with catalytic DMF releases:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: PCl3 converts a carboxylic acid to an acid chloride plus:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: PCl5 gives an acid chloride plus:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Why are SOCl2 and oxalyl chloride preferred?
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: Gases escape as they form, driving the reaction to completion.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Why is a carboxylic acid a poor acylating agent for amines?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Typical pKa of a carboxylic acid:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Which nucleophile converts an acid chloride to an ester?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Which reagent turns an acid chloride into an anhydride?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: How many equivalents of amine are needed for amide formation?
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: One acylates, the second mops up the HCl released.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Why does amide formation consume extra amine?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: What replaces the sacrificial second equivalent of amine?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Why does pyridine not compete with the amine?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Leaving group expelled from an anhydride:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Correct reactivity order?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Standard acetylating agent:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: Reactive enough to acylate directly, stable enough to weigh out in air.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Acetic anhydride acetylates which group of salicylic acid?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: By-product of the aspirin synthesis:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: Half the anhydride leaves unused, which is the atom-economy cost.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Main drawback of acylating with an anhydride:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: One acyl group becomes product, the other becomes waste.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Heating succinic acid gives:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Ring size formed when phthalic acid is heated:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: Diacids that would need a larger ring do not cyclize this way.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: A cyclic anhydride plus an amine first gives:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: The displaced carboxylate stays tethered instead of wandering off.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: An amic acid becomes an imide on treatment with:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: A second intramolecular condensation closes the ring again.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Which of these is an imide?
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: Two acyl groups share one nitrogen rather than one oxygen.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: An acid chloride with AlCl3 ionizes to:

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Friedel-Crafts acylation forms which bond?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: Benzoic acid to phenyl ketone: which reagent is used first?

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: SOCl2 converts alcohols into:
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: One reagent solving the same problem on a different functional group.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: What does SOCl2 do to an OH group?
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: A terrible leaving group is swapped for an excellent one.

acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.q: How does esterification via an acid chloride differ from Fischer?
acyl-chlorides-anhydrides.why: Chloride never comes back, so there is no equilibrium to push.

nitriles.q: Oxidation level of the nitrile carbon:

nitriles.q: Which sits on the same oxidation rung as a nitrile?
nitriles.why: Also three carbon-heteroatom bonds, so interconversion needs no oxidant.

nitriles.q: A nitrile carbon and a carboxylic acid carbon both carry:
nitriles.why: The triple bond to nitrogen supplies all three at once.

nitriles.q: Converting a nitrile into an amide counts as:
nitriles.why: A sideways move along one rung, so no oxidant is required.

nitriles.q: RCH2X plus NaCN gives:

nitriles.q: Mechanism of cyanide with a primary alkyl halide:

nitriles.q: Why is cyanide well suited to this reaction?
nitriles.why: Exactly the combination that favors substitution over elimination.

nitriles.q: Approximate pKa of HCN:
nitriles.why: Weakly basic conjugate base, so elimination is not promoted.

nitriles.q: A tertiary alkyl halide with NaCN gives mainly:
nitriles.why: Backside attack is blocked, so elimination takes over entirely.

nitriles.q: Dehydrating a primary amide gives:
nitriles.why: Another sideways move along the same oxidation rung.

nitriles.q: Which reagents dehydrate a primary amide?
nitriles.why: Both strip water from the amide rather than changing oxidation level.

nitriles.q: A cyanohydrin comes from cyanide plus which of these?
nitriles.why: Addition to the carbonyl leaves an OH on the neighboring carbon.

nitriles.q: The Sandmeyer route to an aryl nitrile starts from:
nitriles.why: CuCN replaces the nitrogen that leaves as N2.

nitriles.q: Why is Sandmeyer the only route to an aryl nitrile?
nitriles.why: There is no electrophilic cyanide reagent for aromatic substitution.

nitriles.q: RCN with aqueous H3O+ and heat gives:
nitriles.why: Base with heat reaches the same product via its carboxylate.

nitriles.q: Nitrile hydrolysis passes through:
nitriles.why: That intermediate is real enough to isolate under mild conditions.

nitriles.q: Mild hydrolysis of a nitrile can be stopped at:
nitriles.why: Stopping early exploits the amide being an intermediate, not a side product.

nitriles.q: LiAlH4 then water converts RCN into:
nitriles.why: Two hydrides are delivered and the nitrogen stays attached.

nitriles.q: Butanenitrile with LiAlH4 gives:

nitriles.q: DIBAL-H, one equivalent at -78 C, converts RCN into:
nitriles.why: Workup hydrolyzes the intermediate rather than reducing it further.

nitriles.q: The species present before DIBAL-H workup is:

nitriles.q: Why does DIBAL-H stop after a single hydride?
nitriles.why: The reagent is crippled by the intermediate, not merely rationed.

nitriles.q: A Grignard on a nitrile, after workup, gives:

nitriles.q: The C-N triple bond stretch appears near:
nitriles.why: Sharp and medium, in a region almost nothing else occupies.

nitriles.q: Why is that nitrile stretch diagnostic?
nitriles.why: Between 2500 and 2000 there is little else to confuse it with.

nitriles.q: RX to RCN to RCOOH accomplishes:
nitriles.why: Cyanide supplies the added carbon, hydrolysis converts it to the acid.

nitriles.q: The Grignard route to a chain-extended acid fails on substrates with:
nitriles.why: Any acidic proton quenches the organometallic reagent.
